title: Why One Broken Part Stops a Business | Principles of Management Ep 12
description:
One morning, Kabir's cash counter breaks down. Customers cannot pay, the queue stops, Asha's chai goes cold and Meena runs out of clean cups. One small part fails, and the whole stall suffers. In this animated lesson we use Ravi's chai stall to understand the systems approach to management, step by step.

You will see where the idea came from: Ludwig von Bertalanffy, the Austrian biologist behind general system theory, and Daniel Katz and Robert Kahn, who applied it to organisations in 1966. We define the systems approach and subsystems, then watch one morning at Chai Corner run through the system loop: inputs, process (transformation), outputs and feedback. We cover the open system on a festival evening, synergy (the whole is greater than the sum of its parts), and see subsystems, interdependence, feedback, open systems and synergy in a hospital, a car factory, an app and a shop today. We also look at the limits honestly: the systems approach gives managers a way to see, not a step by step recipe.

This is Episode 12 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
